questions.prompt: What is the main reason Lightning moves most payments off-chain?

options.label: To avoid Bitcoin block space for routine transfers
To eliminate the need for full nodes

questions.explanation: Lightning channels batch many updates; on-chain settlement is for open/close and disputes.

questions.prompt: What role do BOLTs play in the Lightning ecosystem?

options.label: Optional style guides with no interop impact

questions.explanation: BOLTs define peer protocol, onion format, invoices, and more so LND, CLN, and LDK can interoperate.

questions.prompt: What does a BOLT11 invoice primarily encode?

options.label: A one-time payment request with amount and routing hints

questions.explanation: BOLT11 invoices are payment requests wallets decode before attempting a route.

questions.prompt: How do BOLT12 offers differ from BOLT11 invoices?

options.label: Offers are reusable; invoices are typically one-shot

questions.explanation: Offers support reusable payment flows and modern UX patterns like static QR codes.

questions.prompt: After a typical single-funded channel open, the funder usually starts with:

options.label: No spendable balance until a payment arrives

questions.explanation: The funder's coins sit on their side (outbound). Receiving requires inbound, which often needs a separate strategy.

questions.prompt: What does a revocation key protect against in commitment transactions?

options.label: Invoice expiry on the public graph
Publishing an old channel state after a newer one was agreed

questions.explanation: Revocation lets the honest party penalize a peer who broadcasts a stale commitment.

questions.prompt: What must a hop reveal to settle an HTLC forward?

options.label: The payment preimage matching the payment hash

questions.explanation: HTLCs are hash-locked; the preimage unlocks the conditional payment atomically along the path.

questions.prompt: What is splicing used for?

options.label: Adding or removing capacity without closing the channel

questions.explanation: Splicing adjusts on-chain funding while keeping the channel relationship active.

questions.prompt: In Lightning source-based routing, who typically constructs the payment path?

options.label: The payee before issuing an invoice
Bitcoin miners at block template time

questions.explanation: The sender chooses a path using graph data and hints, then onion-encrypts hop instructions.

questions.prompt: Why can a path fail even when total channel capacity looks sufficient?

options.label: Liquidity may be on the wrong side of one or more hops

questions.explanation: Each forward edge needs outbound on that hop. Wrong-side balance is the common failure mode.

questions.prompt: What does onion routing primarily hide from intermediaries?

options.label: The fact that an HTLC is in flight
The full path and final payee identity beyond their hop

questions.explanation: Sphinx-style onions reveal only the next hop's instructions to each intermediary.

questions.prompt: What is a common production response to uncertain liquidity on the graph?

options.label: Publish exact balances in gossip for every channel
Force close all channels after each failure
Attempt, learn from failures, and retry with updated scores

questions.explanation: Liquidity is not fully public; routers probe and update heuristics (e.g. mission control style).

questions.prompt: Which best describes LND vs LDK?

options.label: LND is a full node daemon; LDK is an embeddable library
LDK only runs on mobile; LND only on servers
They are the same codebase with different names

questions.explanation: LND is commonly operated as a node service; LDK targets app-embedded Lightning.

questions.prompt: What is a typical way to extend Core Lightning (CLN)?
questions.explanation: CLN's plugin architecture is a primary integration path for custom behavior.

questions.prompt: What problem do watchtowers address?

options.label: Finding the cheapest on-chain fee rate
Detecting and responding to breach attempts while a wallet is offline

questions.explanation: Watchtowers help offline users by monitoring for stale state broadcasts.

questions.prompt: Why do LND integrations often use macaroons?

options.label: Scoped API credentials with delegated permissions

questions.explanation: Macaroons let operators grant limited gRPC/REST access without sharing the admin key.

questions.prompt: What makes a Pull project submission meaningful?

options.label: Public repo, working demo path, and evidence a reviewer can verify
A README only with no runnable code
Marking the lesson complete without building

questions.explanation: Projects prove you can ship; reviewers need a repo and evidence on regtest or testnet.

questions.prompt: When should you build a personal tool vs contribute upstream?

options.label: Always contribute before writing any local code
Build to learn deeply; contribute when you have a scoped fix the maintainers want
Never contribute until all roadmaps are complete

questions.explanation: Personal projects deepen understanding; OSS PRs need maintainer-aligned scope.

questions.prompt: Which environment is preferred for Lightning project demos on Pull?

options.label: Mainnet with real funds for every exercise
Regtest or Polar over mainnet for learning

questions.explanation: Local labs are safer and faster for iteration; document how to reproduce.

questions.prompt: Before opening a Lightning PR, you should:

options.label: Open a large refactor without discussion
Skip CI because Lightning is off-chain
Read CONTRIBUTING, find an agreed issue, and run relevant tests

questions.explanation: Maintainers expect scoped changes, tests, and alignment with project norms.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the meaningful-PR rubric?

options.label: Self-check problem fit, scope, correctness, and communication before shipping

questions.explanation: The rubric helps you judge whether a PR is worth a maintainer's time.

questions.prompt: Review Club PRs on Pull are meant to:

options.label: Practice reading real OSS changes tied to what you just learned

questions.explanation: Reviewing curated PRs builds the same skills you need for your own contributions.

questions.prompt: BOLT specification reviews should prioritize:

options.label: Interop, edge cases, rollout behavior, and test vectors

questions.explanation: Spec review keeps the network coherent across implementations.
